content: Croflemer has the potential to inhibit the metabolism of drugs processed by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 at concentrations expected in the gut. However, due to its minimal systemic absorption, it is unlikely to inhibit CYP3A4 systemically. This interaction can lead to increased levels or effects of certain medications, necessitating caution and close monitoring when co-administered. Specific examples include: 1. Lemborexant: Crofelemer may increase lemborexant levels. A lower nightly dose of lemborexant is recommended when used with weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Refer to the drug monograph for dosage adjustments. 2. Levofloxacin: Crofelemer may increase levofloxacin levels by inhibiting gut transporters MRP2 and OATP1A2. Monitor closely. 3. Levonorgestrel (intrauterine and oral): Crofelemer may increase levonorgestrel levels. Monitor for potential effects. 4. Levothyroxine and Liothyronine: Crofelemer may increase levels of these thyroid hormones by inhibiting gut transporters MRP2 and OATP1A2. Monitor closely. 5. Lomitapide: Crofelemer may increase lomitapide levels. Use caution and monitor. 6. Lopinavir: Crofelemer may increase lopinavir levels. Monitor closely. 7. Losartan: Crofelemer may increase losartan levels. Use caution and monitor. 8. Lovastatin: Crofelemer may increase lovastatin levels. Monitor closely. 9. Lurasidone: Crofelemer may increase lurasidone levels. Use caution and monitor. 10. Maraviroc: Crofelemer may increase maraviroc levels. Monitor closely. 11. Medroxyprogesterone: Crofelemer may increase medroxyprogesterone levels. Use caution and monitor. 12. Mefloquine: Crofelemer may increase mefloquine levels. Monitor closely. 13. Metaxalone: Crofelemer may increase metaxalone levels. Use caution and monitor. 14. Methadone: Crofelemer may increase methadone levels. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 15. Methotrexate: Crofelemer may increase methotrexate levels by inhibiting gut transporters MRP2 and OATP1A2. Monitor closely. 16. Methylergonovine: Crofelemer may increase methylergonovine levels. Use caution and monitor. 17. Methylprednisolone: Crofelemer may increase methylprednisolone levels. Monitor closely. 18. Metoclopramide (intranasal): Crofelemer may decrease systemic absorption of metoclopramide when co-administered with drugs impairing GI motility. Monitor for reduced therapeutic effects. 19. Midazolam (oral and intranasal): Crofelemer may increase midazolam levels, potentially prolonging sedation. Use caution and monitor. 20. Mirtazapine: Crofelemer may increase mirtazapine levels.
